helpful_moments.moment: Opening guard disappeared after a stationary FIRE hold with no initial health/shield loss.
Map route and player marker revealed I had overshot Mara; backing up brought up HOLD USE and enabled recovery.
Contextual recovery button and numbered memory markers made collection progress explicit; Sera recovery visibly restored health to 100.
Jump/vault attempts got me past an obstructed approach to a close coil view; coil 1 OFF gave unambiguous damage feedback.

frustrating_moments.moment: Forward movement ended with an enormous wall/sign filling the screen. After strafing and advancing I overshot Mara while damage arrived from offscreen.
Portrait view made hostile identification difficult while navigating. Damage arrows were visible but I rarely had attackers in view. Recovered all memories while largely bypassing combat.

Close coils and structural cover occluded remaining targets. Tried firing/dragging, strafing, backing away and map-assisted reorientation; struggled to retain a clear face and died during the final firing hold.
Many small adjacent lower-screen buttons demand movement, aiming and defensive decisions in a crowded portrait layout. I did not successfully use DASH or phase evades.

failures_and_uncertainties: 5% terminal accuracy indicates poor shot placement in this attempt; it does not isolate aim tuning from reviewer skill, occlusion or the synthetic input method.
A tap at the visible RELOAD button was attempted before opening the first map; a later capture showed full ammo, but automatic behavior and pickup timing prevent attributing that result to the tap.
Jump/vault taps improved approach position; exact individual vault triggering was not independently verified.
Final shot placement and exact lethal attacker were not visible enough to identify reliably.
No observed helper page errors in returned captures; no claim about unobserved errors.
No BUILD80 label was visible on the title screenshot; requested commit remains unverified.

scoring.scale: 0 unusable, 5 playable with substantial friction, 7 good with noticeable issues, 10 exceptional. Scores describe only this one paused synthetic portrait attempt, not a physical-device certification.

reasons.overall_mobile: Playable through all memory objectives with useful planning, but combat aiming and spatial awareness remained difficult and the attempt ended in loss.
reasons.controls: Basic move/fire and contextual use worked; precise aiming, avoiding geometry and coordinating defense were difficult. Dense buttons increase thumb workload; no physical touch ergonomics measured.
reasons.gameplay: Clear recovery progression and coil phase variation, with recoverable navigation mistakes. Offscreen pressure and occluded targets made combat less satisfying in this run.
reasons.presentation: Cohesive dark teal/amber visual identity, atmospheric station and strong title/end panels. Close geometry sometimes reduced the view to walls or black structural surfaces.
reasons.usability: Pausing map, marked routes, changing objectives and contextual use rescued navigation. Frequent map checks were needed and encounter sightlines were hard to maintain.
reasons.readability: Main objectives, health, ammo and terminal stats readable at 390x844. Smaller compass/coil text and lower-screen control density required inspection; visual scene clarity varied.

limitations: Synthetic native touch emulation in Chromium at 390x844, not a physical phone.
